transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I've been having some thoughts lately that are really starting to scare me. 

I've been catching myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And sometimes, like on the drive home from work—I teach secondary school—I just start wondering if my family and my students would be better off without me. 

I don't want to act on it, I really don't, but the fact that my brain is even going there... it scared me enough to make an appointment. I just knew I needed to talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way and having these thoughts—days, weeks, or longer?

It's been going on for a while now. I'd say about a year and seven months. It started right around the time I took on the STEM assessment redesign at school, which was on top of my normal teaching schedule. That's when I first noticed things getting bad.
Over these past 19 months, have you felt down and low pretty much every day without much of a break, or have there been stretches—weeks or months—where your mood actually lifted back to normal?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's... it's kind of hard to look back over that whole time and remember exactly how it fluctuated. The days and weeks just sort of blur together when you're that busy. 

I couldn't really tell you if there were actual stretches where I felt completely back to normal, or if I was just pushing through it to get the work done. I just haven't kept track of it that closely.
During this same period, have there been any stretches of several days where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt more confident and talkative than usual?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've mostly just felt exhausted. I definitely haven't had any bursts of energy or felt like I needed less sleep. If anything, I'm just tired all the time.
Over these past 19 months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?

Yes, I have. I used to really look forward to playing softball, going to my book club, working in my garden... even running the robotics club at school. But now, I mostly just go through the motions if I do show up. A lot of the time I just end up canceling, because none of it really feels enjoyable to me anymore.

Over these 19 months, has your mood stayed pretty much the same level of 'low' the whole time, or have there been certain periods where it became noticeably worse and more intense than your usual baseline?

I don't really think so. It feels like it's just been a pretty steady low the entire time. Like I said, the months kind of blur together with teaching, but... no, I haven't noticed any specific periods where it suddenly got a lot worse or more intense. It's just been this constant, heavy feeling every day.

Before this current period began about 19 months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of feeling this down or losing interest in things, at some earlier point in your life, followed by a return to feeling normal?

No, I don't think I have. Before all this started about a year and a half ago, I was always pretty active and upbeat. I mean, everyone has a bad week here or there, but... no, I've never gone through a stretch where I felt this down or just stopped caring about my hobbies. This is really the first time it's ever been like this.
Over these past 19 months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, such as eating significantly more or less than usual?

Yeah, I have actually. Um, most school days I just... I either forget or just avoid eating until late in the afternoon. I don't really have much of an appetite. And because of that, over the past year, my clothes have gotten noticeably looser. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight or anything, it's just happening because I'm not eating like I used to.
Over these past 19 months, have you had trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making decisions—like when grading papers or planning lessons?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's actually been a big issue at work. When I sit down to grade, I'll read the same student response three or four times and still not know what score to give it. The information just doesn't sink in. And making decisions is just as hard. Even simple choices, um, like trying to figure out which lab supplies to order for a lesson, can stall me for an hour. I just can't seem to focus or make up my mind lately.
Over these past 19 months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yes, my sleep has definitely changed. Even when I'm completely exhausted, I'll just lie awake in bed. My mind keeps replaying upcoming assessment deadlines or little mistakes I made in the classroom that day. And then, when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up around 4 a.m., and I never really get back to sleep after that.
Are you still able to go to work and manage your teaching duties most days, or have these symptoms made it hard for you to function at work or keep up with your usual daily responsibilities?

It's... it's definitely made it hard to function. I'm still going in to work, but I'm falling really behind on my grading and lesson planning, and it's getting to the point where it's affecting my classroom. I actually made a grading mistake recently that kind of scared me, just because I used to be so meticulous about my work. 

And outside of school... I've basically stopped showing up for my friends and family the way I used to. It feels like my whole life has just narrowed down to barely getting through the school day, and then going home completely exhausted.
